reference_protocol.score_100: 100% means every scored target satisfied the specific published test. It does not mean 100% trusted page transcription, historical pronunciation, smith identification or translation.

legacy_protocol.limitations: Native-pixel request conflicts with the documented normalized-coordinate convention. Recorded boxes are scored as returned and are not silently rescaled. This is a failed configuration baseline, not general Qwen kanji accuracy.

final_protocol.conversion: Validate each axis in 0..1000; floor top/left and ceil bottom/right after conversion using native dimensions. Join region text in returned reading order.

intermediate_trial.protocol: normalized1000 with duplicate complete-text and region-text output
intermediate_trial.reason_stopped: First page exhausted the output budget; final finite run requests region text once. Completed raw receipts retained privately and included in shared accounting.

qwen.comparison_limits: Quantized local deployment with this prompt, resolution/token limits and runtime. Protocol was revised after observing failures; no claim to measure all Qwen deployments. Model/server startup excluded from per-page command runtime.

location_diagnostic.observation: Both printed pages are represented, but the returned right header box does not intersect the labelled header. Other occurrences of a word elsewhere on the scan do not satisfy the labelled occurrence. This explains why readable page text can coexist with zero localized-target hits. No post-hoc box adjustment was applied.

upstream_generation_guidance.limitation: Both recorded full-frame protocols instead use temperature 0 and max_tokens 8192; other sampling penalties were not explicitly set in the request. Their scores do not measure the official recommended decoding recipe or best attainable Qwen accuracy. Effect of changing sampling/penalties/output allowance was not measured.

observed_adapter_validation_failures.cause: Model returned six boxes exceeding the requested normalized 0..1000 vertical range; maximum y=1152.
observed_adapter_validation_failures.handling: Adapter rejects the invalid page response; the failed attempt remains in scores. No clipping or reinterpretation was applied.

docs/sword_ocr_method.md.text:
# How the sword library influences OCR

For a scan, NDLOCR-Lite first detects and reads the page. Koshirai keeps that
transcript. The optional `sword-lattice-v1` profile then uses the bundled sword
spellings to disambiguate a bounded set of visually uncertain characters. This
is a different operation from attaching dictionary candidates after recognition.

```text
Scan → native NDLOCR text and regions → original transcript retained
                                  ↓
                     bounded direct line recognition
                                  ↓
                   scored visual character alternatives
                                  ↓
              sword spelling support + preservation checks
                         ↙                    ↘
               proposed substitution       original retained
```

## What may change

The profile examines at most 32 OCR lines containing kanji, prioritizing lines
with more kanji. A direct pass through the pinned 100-character PARSEQ recognizer
must reproduce the original line exactly after removing whitespace. If it does
not, Koshirai abstains. The recognizer must also emit its end-of-sequence token.

For each character it retains the four highest-scoring visual classes. A proposed
substitution must be among those classes, stay within the configured logit gap,
and improve literal sword-spelling support. The API default requires two source
families; SupportingReference publications are grouped together, PrimaryReference publications together,
and dealer sources together. Families are support categories, not established
independent witnesses. Untyped dealer fragments are excluded from this decoder.

Only one character per line may change. Everything else, including whitespace,
remains identical. Known historical-variant pairs and Unicode compatibility
normalizations are excluded. Equally supported conflicting corrections cause
abstention. Native digital text and explicitly reviewed transcripts are not
rewritten by this profile. Unsupported text stays as NDLOCR returned it.

A library spelling can also occur in ordinary Japanese. Its presence does not
prove that this particular occurrence denotes a sword term or identifies a smith.
A proposed reading remains a proposal and needs source/context review. The model
scores are logits, not calibrated probabilities that a transcription is correct.

## Run the measured profile

After `sh setup.sh --install-ocr`, save this configuration outside the checkout:

```json
{"enhancement_config":{"profile":"sword-lattice-v1","max_crops":32,"timeout":90,"min_source_families":1,"max_logit_gap":1.0}}
```

```sh
cli="$KANJI_DATA_DIR/environment/bin/kanji-translator"
"$cli" scan /path/to/scans --config /path/to/sword-profile.json \
  --output "$KANJI_DATA_DIR/outputs/sword-profile"
```

The final confirmation experiment explicitly uses **one source family** and a
maximum gap of **1.0 logit**. The API default is two families when the field is
omitted. The broader earlier pilot used two families and a 2.0-logit gap; its
negative result remains in the evaluation. No additional model, GPU, training
job or remote service is required. The profile changes no default behavior
unless requested. See the [measured results](../benchmarks/sword_ocr_evaluation.json).

Results contain `raw_ndl.txt` and `enhanced.txt`. Each change in `results.jsonl`
retains source/crop hashes, geometry, original and proposed text, model and
library identity, visual alternatives and supporting library records. Competing
candidates and reasons for abstention are retained. Source originals are not
modified, and importing a proposal does not promote it to a human review.

## Establishing whether the library helps

The library-disabled ablation sets `library_enabled:false` in the same profile.
It uses the same source pixels and recognition method, retains the character
scores, and leaves the original text unchanged. Reapplying the decision rule to
identical saved score arrays separately tests that a change depends on the
library rather than another image preprocessing operation.

Accuracy requires source review. A higher library score is not itself a correct
character. The evaluation therefore includes every changed region, reports
corrections and regressions, and retains uncertainty. Unchanged text cancels in
a paired absolute error difference, but a review of changed regions alone does
not supply a whole-page character-error-rate denominator. AI pixel review is
provisional and must not be presented as expert human adjudication.

The older `local-crop-v1` profile remains available to reproduce its recorded
negative experiment. Agreement between its two retries is correlated evidence;
its five-page trial found a deletion regression. It is not the sword-prior method
described here. See the [blind trial](blind_researcher_review.md),
[benchmark protocol](../benchmarks/README.md) and [README](../README.md).

docs/ocr_and_enrichment.md.text:
# What Koshirai does

The default reader is **NDLOCR-Lite followed by Koshirai lookup**. NDLOCR-Lite
uses learned layout and recognition models to produce text and native-pixel
regions. Koshirai preserves that transcription, attaches its source identity,
and adds core Japanese dictionary and sword-library candidates. It also retains
unrecognized material as unresolved regions. Native usable PDF text takes
precedence over raster recognition.

Koshirai is therefore a deterministic evidence and enrichment layer around a
model-based OCR reader. Its bundled sword dataset is a lookup resource, not
fine-tuned neural weights. Installing it does not train NDLOCR or Qwen. The
optional Tesseract backend remains available for explicit comparisons or other
collections; it is not a silent fallback when NDLOCR fails.

A recognized spelling can have several readings, meanings or historical smiths.
An exact spelling match, an attested variant, and a source's printed romanization
are different kinds of evidence. Keep their citations and alternatives. A
candidate appearing in several derived sources is not necessarily independent
corroboration. Neither dictionary coverage nor an OCR engine score is a calibrated
probability that a particular historical person or translation is correct.

For example, a source region reading 刄文 should retain 刄文 in its literal field.
An attested variant relation may retrieve 刃文 and a cited reading such as hamon.
That lookup does not authorize rewriting the page or identifying a smith. A
lexical English gloss describes a word sense; it does not translate the whole
sentence. Missing or contradictory evidence should remain visible.

## Benchmark interpretation

The [public benchmark](../benchmarks/README.md) compares observed page-reader
outputs on the same random frames. Its reviewed targets are incomplete. A score
of 100% means every target included in that metric passed its stated rule; it
does not imply that every character or region on each page is correct. Unlabeled
omissions and hallucinations can still exist. Candidate-support scores test
whether a cited acceptable alternative is available, not whether the system
selected the correct reading, identity or fluent translation.

The benchmark was used to select the default reader. It is now development and
regression evidence. The reference erratum and both score versions are retained.
Accuracy qualification needs a separate, held-out set with independently reviewed
source text, complete region labels and adjudicated reading/meaning alternatives.
Keep uncertain targets explicit or exclude them from the affected denominator;
do not turn an AI's best guess into a supposedly perfect answer key.

## What a confidence percentage would mean

A probability can be useful, but it must name the event being predicted. The
chance that an image contains a particular glyph is different from the chance
that a word has a particular reading, or that a signature identifies a particular
smith. The current library returns cited candidates and unresolved alternatives;
it does not produce calibrated probabilities for those events. The benchmark's
113 matching targets out of 140 are word/name occurrences, not 113 characters
with 95% confidence.

Character accuracy could exceed exact word accuracy: one wrong glyph makes a
whole word fail an exact-match check. The present target score cannot quantify
that difference, especially where a missed region supplies no transcription.

A future candidate ranker could combine visible stroke evidence, surrounding
text, attested spellings and competing OCR proposals. Commonness supplies a
prior; it cannot override a missing or contradictory stroke. Several dictionaries
or readers may share sources and errors, so their agreement must not be counted
as independent confirmation automatically. Keep the literal OCR alongside any
proposed correction and retain an unknown/other alternative.

Until tested, a number such as 70% would be an uncalibrated model estimate. To
make it a defensible probability, collect separately reviewed pages, group
predictions by estimated confidence, and compare each group's estimate with its
observed correctness. Approximately 95% of predictions in a 95% group should be
correct, with the sample count and uncertainty reported. Check ordinary text,
rare sword vocabulary and historical glyphs separately. Review uncertainty in
the answer key remains separate from uncertainty in the reader's prediction.

Reference confidence can be graded too: distinguish clear printed glyphs,
ambiguous inscriptions and uncertain historical readings. Assign those grades
from source evidence and independent review before examining predictions. An OCR
match must not itself promote a reference to high confidence. Any future weighted
score should publish its weighting rule and the unweighted counts alongside it;
subjective weights do not turn provisional labels into verified ground truth.

## Whether to train a model

The current engineering recommendation is to use the measured NDLOCR-plus-lookup
baseline first. Do not train an eight-billion-parameter model merely to memorize
the lookup library. Correct source facts, citations and alternative readings can
be updated through ordinary data pull requests without changing OCR weights.

A future training experiment should address a demonstrated residual problem:
rare historical glyph recognition, difficult page segmentation, or selection
among context-dependent readings. Those are separate evaluation tasks. Use
rights-cleared source images with reviewed labels; split by publication and
smith/source lineage to reduce leakage. Preserve the current benchmark as
regression data and reserve new publications for final evaluation.

Fine-tuning for stroke and font recognition needs image crops paired with verified
literal transcriptions. Kanji-to-romaji tables alone do not teach visual shape.
Useful cases include historical typefaces, small distinguishing strokes, faint
ink and overlapping annotations. Preserve the observed historical form in the
label; keep modern equivalents in separate lookup fields. Check crop resolution
and layout extraction before attributing every error to missing model training.
Also test the model's official inference settings: this pilot's greedy Qwen
decoding and output ceiling differ from its published VL generation guidance.

One useful next experiment is NDLOCR layout followed by Qwen or Sol inspection of
difficult crops, with cited dictionary alternatives supplied separately. This
avoids asking a full-page vision response to solve every location and reading at
once. It is a proposed architecture, not a measured system in this benchmark;
test it on new reviewed pages before claiming an accuracy improvement.

If glyph recognition is the main error, compare a smaller recognition-model
adaptation before committing to a Qwen vision-language fine-tune. If contextual
reading selection remains the problem, test Qwen as a separate proposal stage.
Measure errors, abstentions, fabricated text, region alignment, memory and time
against the same baseline. Keep its proposed correction separate from literal OCR
and require source review before promotion. No model training is included in this
release.

## Which Qwen model was tested

The benchmark uses **Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct**, a vision-language model, rather than
the text-only Qwen3-8B. The official weights tested here are not a Koshirai or
kanji-only fine-tune. Q4_K_M describes weight quantization, not additional
Japanese training.

Qwen's [technical report](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.21631v1) describes a visual
encoder connected to the Qwen3 language model, with multilingual OCR training
from collected, synthetic and pseudo-labelled image/text data. That training
teaches visual/text relationships; loading a kanji dictionary at inference time
does not update those weights. The report does not establish accuracy on this
Fujishiro sample. Consult the [official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct)
and the benchmark's exact quantized runtime pins when comparing results.

Upstream reader implementation and model notices:
[NDLOCR-Lite](https://github.com/ndl-lab/ndlocr-lite). Koshirai's tests and observed
benchmark results establish only the behavior documented with their receipts.

# Independent five-page researcher trial

The clean README installation, both scan modes and corpus import succeeded. The local crop profile did **not** improve the frozen reference score. Pixel review of every actual changed region found one information-loss regression, one formatting-only change and one unresolved glyph/encoding change. These are **provisional AI-reviewed findings**, not human-certified accuracy or full-book qualification.

This worker used **gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning**, with no prior project context. It received only a read-only repository snapshot and its task instructions. Isolation was instruction-based on the same host, **not an OS sandbox**. It did not consult previous outputs, other project folders or existing installations. One host process listing incidentally exposed unrelated command-line paths; those were not opened or used. The application used no keys, private source data or remote model calls. The worker made no source modifications and created no subagents, commits or publication.

## Selection and source receipts

Seed: `079d46f24a2dfdbaa8ef53d0ce500e41` (fresh 128-bit system-random seed). The documented `benchmarks/sample_holdout.py` ranked every eligible `(pid,frame)` by SHA256(`seed:pid:frame`) and froze the first five before download. All development `(pid,frame)` pairs and duplicate development image hashes were excluded. The population was 639 frames across the four documented editions before development exclusions. These are new frames from development editions, **not new-source generalization**. All five downloads succeeded; no resampling occurred. Source attribution: 国立国会図書館 / National Diet Library, JAPAN; repository source metadata marks these editions PDM. The precise metadata remains in `frozen-sample.json`.

| ID | Public source | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| ndl-1116191-0223 | [NDL image](https://dl.ndl.go.jp/api/iiif/1116191/R0000223/full/full/0/default.jpg) | `a81c2a7c585cda4723b080157fea02dc644a169a6761d67b2fa274961a5f9c91` |
| ndl-1116191-0211 | [NDL image](https://dl.ndl.go.jp/api/iiif/1116191/R0000211/full/full/0/default.jpg) | `4d17aef436fec6d311f4b84f429c7d0023384f6becf3c0a5c55eb903b57baa26` |
| ndl-1116200-0228 | [NDL image](https://dl.ndl.go.jp/api/iiif/1116200/R0000228/full/full/0/default.jpg) | `7b1a58e6714e8ade7053e1d56fc7ea6a07b7ed67da8cddc8dcec66b22d558b9d` |
| ndl-1116191-0129 | [NDL image](https://dl.ndl.go.jp/api/iiif/1116191/R0000129/full/full/0/default.jpg) | `30380ec0edb5f1f3beac53156adc5dd93fbe33c218d4960d025df8326d23ce96` |
| ndl-1116191-0035 | [NDL image](https://dl.ndl.go.jp/api/iiif/1116191/R0000035/full/full/0/default.jpg) | `9e3df793a63090ff7623a5f7cd761f9a4fd075e4ba93b05f81ee2f4c17a19058` |

## References and scoring

Before starting either scan or viewing any OCR output, the worker viewed all five source images and froze two short readable spans per page: ten spans, **63 characters**. These deliberately small, relatively easy anchors are not a representative complete transcript. The freeze, source locations, timestamp and hash are retained in `frozen-references.json` and `frozen-references.sha256`. References were never revised after viewing output.

Score: remove whitespace only; keep all other Unicode distinctions literal. For each reference, calculate its minimum Levenshtein distance to any substring of that page's transcript (free transcript prefix/suffix). Also count exact reference containment. This is an **optimistic anchor diagnostic**, not spatially aligned full-page CER: duplicate text elsewhere could satisfy an anchor. The eight exact matches were located in the intended page's text; one inscription anchor may also appear in printed descriptive text, so its exact hit alone cannot establish that its carved pixels were read. The analysis reports edit counts rather than certifying character accuracy.

| Reference | Page ID | Frozen text | Baseline edits | Enhanced edits |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| r01 | ndl-1116191-0223 | 重國南紀四代 | 0 | 0 |
| r02 | ndl-1116191-0223 | 重康上總大掾 | 0 | 0 |
| r03 | ndl-1116191-0211 | 菊平伊賀守 | 0 | 0 |
| r04 | ndl-1116191-0211 | 行長高田 | 0 | 0 |
| r05 | ndl-1116200-0228 | 天文九年十二月吉日 | 9 | 9 |
| r06 | ndl-1116200-0228 | 大永三年十二月吉日 | 9 | 9 |
| r07 | ndl-1116191-0129 | 國輝和泉大掾初代 | 0 | 0 |
| r08 | ndl-1116191-0129 | 伊勢守國輝 | 0 | 0 |
| r09 | ndl-1116191-0035 | 兼中武藏守 | 0 | 0 |
| r10 | ndl-1116191-0035 | 兼氏志津三郎 | 0 | 0 |

Both modes recover **8/10 exact spans**, with **18/63 minimum-substring edit errors (28.57%)**. The two nine-character inscription references on `ndl-1116200-0228` are absent from both transcripts; that page's OCR consists almost entirely of margin headings and folio text. The minimum-distance tie resolves to the empty substring for those references, so the 18 edits are deletion diagnostics, not a uniquely aligned error breakdown. Enhancement neither recovers those inscriptions nor changes the eight exact hits.

## Complete paired result and changed-region review

Each run processed **5 pages / 234 regions**, with **0 errors**, **0 unlocated OCR regions**, and **114 unresolved regions**. Both scan exit statuses were 0. Baseline original transcripts exactly match the originals preserved by the enhanced run. The documented profile used `max_crops:4`, `timeout:60`, `crop_timeout:15`. It recorded **3 changes and 17 abstentions**. A direct comparison of all paired enrichment regions found exactly those same three changes; every changed source crop was inspected in its native orientation, with enlarged glyph review as needed. The review images and hash-bound crop/model attempts remain available in local artifacts and full results.

| Source / region | Original | Enhanced proposal | Provisional category |
|---|---|---|---|
| ndl-1116191-0035.jpg / `page:0:line:2` | `【か】兼中・兼永・兼氏・兼植五〇` | `兼中・兼永・兼氏・兼植` | regression |
| ndl-1116191-0211.jpg / `page:0:line:0` | `【き―ゆ】 菊平・鬼洞庵―行周・行長` | `【き-ゆ】菊平・鬼洞庵-行周・行長` | formatting_only_uncertain |
| ndl-1116200-0228.jpg / `page:0:line:2` | `【す】 祐定` | `【す】祐定` | glyph_uncertain |

1. The first crop visibly contains the kana heading and bottom folio. Removing them loses source information. The baseline folio transcription may also be wrong; this does not turn deletion into an accuracy gain.
2. The second edit changes long separators to ASCII hyphens and drops a space. The vertical source stroke does not uniquely establish a Unicode dash. No lexical correction was demonstrated.
3. The third edit changes `祐` to `祐`, plus spacing. The compatibility/unified encoding distinction is not established by these pixels. It remains uncertain rather than an improvement.

No changed region is counted as a demonstrated accuracy improvement. Shared-model retry agreement and dictionary candidate counts were not used as correctness evidence. Retained problems include the two missing inscription lines, the visible-header deletion, glyph uncertainty, and the unchanged 114 unresolved regions. The remaining page text was not fully transcribed or certified.

## End-to-end corpus result

Baseline import: **234 added, 0 existing**. Enhanced import: **3 added, 231 existing**. Repeat enhanced import: **0 added, 234 existing**. The corpus contains **237 observations**, including **3 with preserved original and enhanced text**, and **0 human reviews**. There was no automatic promotion or sharing. Imports verified the source hashes. These results establish local corpus retention and repeat-import idempotence for this run, not accuracy.

## Reproduction

`$WORK` denotes a fresh external directory. The original run used a read-only snapshot at `$WORK/repository`, an initially absent `$WORK/app`, and empty dedicated pip, Hugging Face and XDG caches. Python **3.12.3**, Python venv/pip support, POSIX shell, HTTPS access and sufficient disk were already available (374 GB free at start). No sudo or OS package changes occurred. Installer-created pip build staging can use normal host temporary directories; the dedicated caches were initially empty. App and OCR dependency lists are retained as `run-logs/app-packages.txt` and `run-logs/ocr-packages.txt`.

The following are the substantive original commands, expressed with `$WORK` in place of the original absolute trial root. Use a new directory to avoid intentional frozen-selection/output overwrite protections. The local `run.sh` records the exact originally executed scan/import sequence. Artifact filenames in this report refer to retained external trial evidence, not files bundled in the repository.

```sh
export WORK=/path/to/fresh/trial
export KANJI_DATA_DIR="$WORK/app"
export KANJI_CACHE_DIR="$WORK/app/cache"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$WORK/empty-home/cache"
export PIP_CACHE_DIR="$WORK/empty-home/pip"
export HF_HOME="$WORK/empty-home/huggingface"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
mkdir -p "$WORK/run-logs" "$WORK/empty-home"
cd "$WORK/repository"
python3 --version
df -h /tmp
sh setup.sh --install-ocr > "$WORK/run-logs/setup.log" 2>&1
python="$WORK/app/environment/bin/python"
cli="$WORK/app/environment/bin/kanji-translator"
"$python" -B benchmarks/sample_holdout.py \
  --seed 079d46f24a2dfdbaa8ef53d0ce500e41 --count 5 \
  --output "$WORK/frozen-sample.json" --images "$WORK/source-images" \
  > "$WORK/run-logs/sample.log" 2>&1
# Inspect source images and freeze the exact references above BEFORE OCR.
printf '%s\n' '{"enhancement_config":{"profile":"local-crop-v1","max_crops":4,"timeout":60,"crop_timeout":15}}' > "$WORK/enhancement.json"
export TMPDIR="$WORK/app/cache"
"$python" -m pip freeze > "$WORK/run-logs/app-packages.txt"
"$WORK/app/ndlocr/environment/bin/python" -m pip freeze > "$WORK/run-logs/ocr-packages.txt"
"$cli" scan "$WORK/source-images" --output "$WORK/baseline" > "$WORK/run-logs/baseline.log" 2>&1
"$cli" scan "$WORK/source-images" --config "$WORK/enhancement.json" \
  --output "$WORK/enhanced" > "$WORK/run-logs/enhanced.log" 2>&1
for kind in baseline enhanced; do
  printf '{"source_dir":"%s/source-images","results":"%s/%s/results.jsonl"}\n' "$WORK" "$WORK" "$kind" | \
    "$cli" corpus-ingest > "$WORK/run-logs/corpus-$kind.json"
done
printf '{"source_dir":"%s/source-images","results":"%s/enhanced/results.jsonl"}\n' "$WORK" "$WORK" | \
  "$cli" corpus-ingest > "$WORK/run-logs/corpus-repeat.json"
printf '{"limit":1}\n' | "$cli" corpus-inspect > "$WORK/run-logs/corpus-inspect.json"
```

The installer fetched NDLOCR-Lite **1.3.0**, upstream revision `df90b226e6f568bf0df32f12b935118d6cb74329`; `app/ndlocr/installation.json` preserves its model/config/dependency hashes. Live dictionaries can change on future installs: this run's JMdict hash was `5af39046e9579fd5e14d07a048fccce422b8df0d940ba8c086439e5a7617eab6`, JMnedict `01155974dde819eb1f37caf0420698ad685df927c3c18a52223b73710b3c287d`, and KANJIDIC2 `0ed6f22aebeb1f9cef9b69f2f05407822ca69ed6a8be86fabb74c25eabcfe8fd`. Preserved downloaded assets and hashes are needed for byte-identical reproduction; another fresh live installation is not guaranteed identical.

Read-only inspections used `cat`, `rg`, `head`, `tail`, `ls`, `df`, a process listing, Python JSON/SQLite/hash inspection and source-image viewing. No independent machine transcript of every inspection command was captured; substantive reproduction commands, installer/package logs, original driver, frozen manifests, source hashes, full output receipts and analysis evidence are retained. All 104 files in the tested repository snapshot retained their original hashes. Subsequent release documentation was not part of that snapshot. This trial does not establish enhanced OCR superiority; human adjudication and larger, spatially aligned references remain outstanding.

## Frozen evidence identities

The five-page selection SHA-256 is `4bb6b68c5e8f649768fc23c0457d901f81b0092dbfc123f03eafb16f68fc6f5b`; the pre-output reference JSON SHA-256 is `1298c786bbdcaf3c50aaf3c0287be80e372cb09924072ffc8ca2ebe25b359707`. The tables above expose the source IDs, bytes and reference text needed to audit this small diagnostic.
